NFL.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, its side wins about as often as Vegas's chances say, which is less than half the time.
NFL.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games this season where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won. Past-season test: the model's side won 47.4% in 2010-2019 (Vegas 42.9%) and 42.9% in 2020-2025 (Vegas 43.3%), so no edge over Vegas's own chances. HOU at CLE is this week's case.
NFL.test: Check results of the attached check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025 against Vegas's chances; add up this season's cases until there are 20+.

test_result.note: Won 43% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 43%, about what Vegas's own chances said, so there's no edge.

NFL.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
NFL.evidence: Past-season test says the model's side with a 4+ point gap won 48.3% in 2020-2025 (174 games, 4 pushes), below break-even; no 2010-2019 data. This season, the over/under is 30-24 overall and went 10-4 in the last two weeks, so the small sample does not show the same weakness. L9 (gap 5.3) fits this group.
NFL.test: Compare gap groups under 2, 2-4 and 4+ on past seasons; keep tracking this season's 4+ gap games until 20+.

test_result.note: Won 48.3% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

NFL.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
NFL.evidence: 9 of the 16 games where the winner was wrong through Week 9 named efficiency as the main reason (not updated for the WAS-NYG miss, which had no named driver). Newest misses: JAX-BAL off by 17.5 and HOU-LAC by 18.1, with no stat explaining most of it.
NFL.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

NFL.lesson: Long-shot picks (underdog winners and big-game props) hit a bit below the model's chances and lose units.
NFL.evidence: Underdog picks are 5 of 19 against 7.7 expected (-6.54 units). Big-game picks are 12 of 36 against 11.8 expected (-8.99 units), so the loss is mostly from prices. Milestone picks are 31 of 40 against 29.9 expected (-3.29 units).
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for underdog winners and long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

NFL.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running a little below the model's chances.
NFL.evidence: 12 of 24 best-value picks hit this season, against 12.7 expected, at -1.09 units. The gap is under 1 hit. This week's five value picks sit only 0.4 to 1.0 points over break-even.
NFL.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks per edge group.

NFL.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
NFL.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.7 for the model vs 9.0 for Vegas over 56 graded games; the model is 25-31-1 against the spread (7-9 in the last two weeks). Past-season test of the model's spread side: 51.9% in 2010-2019 and 48.9% in 2020-2025 across 1,660 games. That is below the 52.4% break-even, so no edge.
NFL.test: Compare average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week and season, before changing anything.

test_result.note: Won 48.9% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

NFL.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas on games with a QB change are not clearly misses by the model.
NFL.evidence: Earlier cases: DAL at PHI, PHI at WAS (Hurts on IR) and MIN (Murray out, Wentz in). Past-season test of the model's spread side with a QB change and a 3+ point gap: 54.2% in 2010-2019 (203 games) and 54.4% in 2020-2025 (160 games). That is above break-even but short of the 54.5% needed to count as an edge. This week BAL, ARI, MIA, SEA, LV and CLE have QB changes.
NFL.test: Track this season's cases until 20+; compare the model's margin error in QB-change games with all others.

test_result.note: Won 54.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

NFL.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen a little short of the model's chances, but this looks like luck.
NFL.evidence: 16 of 24 hit this season vs 17.4 expected (-3.27 units). Past-season test: the model's side at 70%+ when it agrees with Vegas won 80.4% in 2010-2019 (Vegas 77.1%) and 77.8% in 2020-2025 (Vegas 77.1%), so about what Vegas's chances said. The 1.4-hit shortfall is within normal swings, so this lesson is retired.
NFL.test: No further test needed unless the shortfall grows past 20+ picks per bucket.

test_result.note: Won 78% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 77%, about what Vegas's own chances said, so there's no edge.

College.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up, and the model's totals picks overall have lost more than they won.
College.evidence: Weeks 8-10: over hit in about 16 of 39 such games (41%). Season totals picks are now 109-128 (46%); the Week 11 results shown went 4-3 (Memphis, Ohio, Bowling Green, Western Michigan overs hit; Central Michigan, Buffalo, Toledo missed). Louisiana had no pick.
College.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Also compare the model's and Vegas's average total error. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

College.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes, but efficiency still leads.
College.evidence: Week 10, 26 of the 40 results shown missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 14, finishing drives 5, turnovers 4, nothing stood out 2, defensive/return touchdowns 1. Week 9 had efficiency first in 7 of 26; Week 8 in 15 of 25. Week 11 results had no reviews yet. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
College.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin, defensive/return touchdowns and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

College.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, this season has gone badly, but past seasons say the model's side holds up.
College.evidence: This season about 4 of 14 right (earlier 4 of 12; Week 11 added Ohio-Miami (OH), Miami (OH) won 34-17, and Week 10 had Western Kentucky-Middle Tennessee, Middle Tennessee won 51-42; both went to Vegas). Built-in test: the model's side won 47% in 2020-2025 against Vegas's 41%. Eight such games this week (Auburn, Syracuse, Wake Forest, UAB, Arkansas State, Arizona State, Ole Miss, App State), so mo…
College.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

College.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
College.evidence: Season: 12 of 30 hit against 15.3 expected, at -7.09 units. The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on all five picks this week. Two of this week's spread picks (San José State +12.5, Purdue +17.5) sit against the model's own margin (Air Force by 21.1, Iowa by 26.6), so the cover chances need checking.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: Underdog picks have hit a bit less often than the model expected, but long prices have kept units positive.
College.evidence: Season: 10 of 29 hit against 11.5 expected, at +1.56 units. No new underdog results since last run. A few hits swing the units a lot, which shows how much luck is in this list.
College.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

College.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
College.evidence: Season: 23 of 25 hit against 22.4 expected, at +0.49 units (was 22 of 24; 1 of 1 new). Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's over the season, and favorites have covered a lot lately.
College.evidence: Season (about 242 games): average spread miss 12.4 for the model against 11.8 for Vegas, a 0.6 gap. Winners right in 161 of 242 (66.5%), spread record 112-124-4. In the 8 Week 11 results shown the model was 1-7 against the spread and the Vegas favorite covered in 7 of 8.
College.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, whether the gap changes by week of season, and whether favorites cover more often in November.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

College.lesson: When the model's margin for a favorite is 3+ points bigger than Vegas's, it has covered more often than not in the recent results, which clashes with the built-in test.
College.evidence: By my count in the Week 10-11 results shown, about 9 of 14 such games covered (Toledo, Liberty, Louisville, Jacksonville State, Boise State, North Texas, UAB, Wake Forest, Arizona State; Navy, Ohio State, Kansas, Mississippi State, Hawai'i did not). College.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's margin for the favorite exceeds Vegas's by 3+ and check how often the favorite covers, split by size of spread and by week. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.
